profile.reading:
Centeris SH2 Build-to-Suit is the second, larger building on Centeris' South Hill data center campus in Puyallup, Washington, an 86 acre site owned and operated by The Benaroya Company roughly 35 miles south of downtown Seattle. A November 2, 2017 Data Center Frontier article describes this building as a 176,000 square foot powered shell, distinct from the smaller, already operating 56,000 square foot LEED Gold SH1 building on the same campus, this registry's separate SH1 Colocation row, with an on-site substation supporting up to 50 megawatts of total campus capacity between the two buildings. This registry's own earlier research had flagged this row as a distinct, planned or future phase building given the powered shell description, consistent with that same trade press characterization. A more recent October 22, 2025 Data Center Dynamics report on the campus, referring to it as the South Hill Business and Technology Center at 1023 39th Avenue Southeast, Puyallup, Washington 98374, states current owner Centeris invested nearly 200 million dollars over the prior 18 months to expand the campus to 24 megawatts of critical load including liquid cooled racks for AI and cloud customers, though the report does not specify whether that expansion capital built out this specific SH2 shell or expanded capacity within the existing SH1 building, so this row's own build-out status as of the most recent sourcing remains uncertain rather than assumed complete. An earlier Seattle Times feature on the campus describes it as the first transpacific data hub designed to store and connect data between Asia and the US West Coast, built in 2008 and remodeled in 2011 in partnership with network provider Wave, totaling 376,000 square feet across its two buildings. The Benaroya Company is a Pacific Northwest real estate firm with more than 60 years in the region and 100 percent ownership of Centeris.

City of Puyallup planning records add a further local government data point for this campus. In February 2022, an application was filed with the city, case PLCPR20220026, covering an 86.67 acre parcel on 39th Avenue Southeast bounded on the east by Pierce College, a description matching the same South Hill campus this row sits on. The filing described the property's current uses as office, warehouse, and data center, and proposed a rezone from Business and Industrial Park designations to a Mixed Use Center with Urban Center zoning that would have allowed residential and more flexible office, warehouse, and technology uses. City records show the application was cancelled at the applicant's own request in May 2022, so the rezone never proceeded, and the campus has continued operating under its existing data center use since. Washington's own 2026 legislative tax preference review separately lists Benaroya Capital as holding one exemption for the Centeris Puyallup data center under the state's urban data centers sales and use tax program, describing that facility as opened in 2011.

reading.body:
Centeris SH2 Build-to-Suit is a 176,000 square foot powered shell on the 86-acre South Hill campus near Puyallup, Washington, roughly 35 miles south of Seattle. The campus is owned and operated by Centeris, which is wholly owned by The Benaroya Company, a Pacific Northwest real estate firm. SH2 is the second building on this site, distinct from the already operating SH1 facility. As of October 2025, the campus operator invested nearly 200 million dollars over the prior 18 months to expand to 24 megawatts of critical load capacity across both buildings, including liquid cooled racks for AI and cloud customers, though the report does not specify whether this expansion built out SH2 or expanded SH1, leaving SH2's build-out status as of late 2025 uncertain.

The campus was designed in 2008 and remodeled in 2011 to function as a transpacific data hub connecting Asia to the US West Coast, with an on-site substation supporting up to 50 megawatts of total campus capacity. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the published 24 megawatts of critical load represents roughly 600 racks, assuming no other workloads share that power budget. SH2's specific share of that 24 megawatts is not published.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only 2 publish power capacity figures, totaling 60 megawatts. The South Hill campus ranks third in the state by published megawatts, though this ranking reflects the entire campus, not SH2 alone. The grid impact of this site depends on whether SH2 remains a powered shell awaiting tenants or has already been built out as part of the 24-megawatt expansion; this cannot be determined from published sources.
